name: Sihon and Og
charge: Refusing Israel passage and coming out to battle against them
summary: Israel asked only to pass through on the king's highway, turning neither to the right nor to the left. Sihon gathered his people and came out to fight, and Og after him. Both kingdoms were given into Israel's hand, and the land east of Jordan became the first inheritance.
offense: Moses sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites with words of peace (Deuteronomy 2:26): let me pass through thy land (Numbers 21:22); we will not turn into the fields or the vineyards. Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass, but gathered all his people and fought at Jahaz (Numbers 21:23). Og king of Bashan came out against them at Edrei (Deuteronomy 3:1), the last of the remnant of giants (Deuteronomy 3:11).
judgment: Israel smote Sihon with the edge of the sword (Numbers 21:24) and possessed his land from Arnon to Jabbok. Of Og the Lord said, Fear him not, for I have delivered him into thy hand (Numbers 21:34); they smote him and his sons and all his people until none was left him alive (Numbers 21:35). The psalms remember it as mercy that endureth for ever (Psalms 136:17): who smote great kings, and gave their land for an heritage (Psalms 136:21).

entries.commentary: King Arad the Canaanite, which dwelt in the south, fought against Israel and took some of them prisoners. Israel vowed a vow unto the Lord, and the Lord hearkened and delivered up the Canaanites, and Israel utterly destroyed them and their cities. The Canaanites are identified in this teaching with the people called Africans today. The place was called Hormah, which means utter destruction, because that is exactly what Israel did to them there.

They journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea to compass the land of Edom, and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way: since Edom refused passage, Israel had to go around, and the way was longer than they wanted it to be. The people spake against God and against Moses: no bread, no water, and our soul loatheth this light bread. The bread they were loathing was angels' bread, and they complained about it anyway. No other nation on this earth takes food as seriously as Israel; even the complaints over bread and water are a familiar mark of this people to this day. You cannot put another nation in these scriptures.

The Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, and much people of Israel died. Read it with the nation in view: the people being bitten, the people dying, all of it is Israel. Once the serpents started biting and much people died, the people came back into the spirit: we have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord and against thee; pray unto the Lord that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people. Moses made a serpent of brass and set it upon a pole, and it came to pass that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived. The symbol on ambulances today, a snake wrapped around a pole, comes from this scripture. That brass serpent on the pole was for the Israelites, to heal the Israelites, because it was the Israelites being bitten for rebelling against God and against Moses. Christ brought this same passage to Nicodemus. Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, and he came to Christ, who is also a Jew: two Israelites speaking together about the history of Israel. As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel.

The children of Israel set forward and pitched in Oboth, then in Ijeabarim, in the wilderness before Moab toward the sunrising, then in the valley of Zared, then on the other side of Arnon, which is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites. Now Israel comes among the Moabites and the Ammonites, identified in this teaching with the nations called the Chinese and the Japanese today. It is said in the book of the wars of the Lord what he did in the Red Sea and in the brooks of Arnon.

From thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the Lord spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water. Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, O well. The princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver. The recording ends here, during this passage. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

Israel compassed mount Seir many days, and the Lord said, ye have compassed this mountain long enough; turn you northward and pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau, which dwell in Seir, the people called the white man today. They shall be afraid of you: the Most High put fear upon Esau so they would not trouble Israel, because he did not want a war; take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore, and meddle not with them. Mount Seir was given unto Esau for a possession, not so much as a foot breadth of it for Israel; the promise to Israel was the land of Canaan. Israel could buy meat and water of them for money, but take nothing. The Lord thy God hath blessed thee; these forty years he hath been with thee, and thou hast lacked nothing.

Passing from the children of Esau, the same order came concerning Moab: distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle, for Ar was given unto the children of Lot for a possession. For Lot's sake the Most High secured that land to his children; it was not Israel's to conquer.

The Emims dwelt in that land in times past, a people great and many and tall as the Anakims, accounted giants; and the Horims dwelt in Seir beforetime, and the children of Esau succeeded them and dwelt in their stead. That is heavy: the Moabites are not the chosen people, yet they went into a land of giants and took it. Israel had the Most High on their side, the pillar, the power, the angels, and still found a way to be scared of giants.

From Kadesh-barnea to the crossing of the brook Zered was thirty and eight years, until all the generation of the men of war were wasted out from among the host, as the Lord sware unto them. The hand of the Lord was against them to destroy them from among the host until they were consumed; only when all the men of war were dead did the word come to pass over.

Coming over against the children of Ammon, the same charge stood: distress them not, nor meddle with them, for that land was given unto the children of Lot for a possession. Esau, Moab, and Ammon were all off limits; the Most High appointed their possessions, and Israel was to pick no fight with them.

Ammon's land was also accounted a land of giants: the Zamzummims, a people great and many and tall as the Anakims; and the Lord destroyed them, and the Ammonites succeeded them and dwelt in their stead. The giants were famous from the beginning, of great stature and expert in war, yet the Lord chose them not and gave them no knowledge; they were destroyed because they had no wisdom and perished through their own foolishness. There are no giants today; stature and skill in war saved none of them.

As he did to the children of Esau when he destroyed the Horims from before them, so these nations succeeded the giants and dwelt in their stead even unto this day. The Avims which dwelt in Hazerim, even unto Azzah, the Caphtorims destroyed them and dwelt in their stead; the Most High moves nations in and out of lands as he wills.

Rise up, pass over the river Arnon: behold, I have given into thine hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle. This recaps [Numbers 21](/bible/numbers/21), when it was time to destroy the king of the Amorites. This day will I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the nations under the whole heaven. The Most High never gave Israel the spirit of fear, but when it was time to conquer he put the fear of Israel on the nations, so they trembled and were in anguish.

Moses sent messengers unto Sihon with words of peace: let me pass through thy land by the highway, buying meat and water of thee for money, only passing through on my feet, as was done passing Esau in Seir and Moab in Ar. But Sihon would not let Israel pass, for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand. It is the same dealing as with Pharaoh: the Lord hardened his heart so the judgment could land, for the iniquity of the Amorites was full and their land was appointed to Israel.

Sihon came out against Israel to fight at Jahaz, and the Lord delivered him: they smote him and his sons and all his people, took all his cities, and utterly destroyed the men, women, and little ones of every city; none was left to remain. That is how thorough the judgment of the Most High was for Israel's sake; that is how specially privileged Israel was, and still they struggled to believe and obey him. Only the cattle and the spoil of the cities were taken for a prey. From Aroer by the brink of the river of Arnon even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong: the Lord our God delivered all unto us. Only the land of the children of Ammon they came not unto, nor unto whatsoever the Lord our God forbad: Israel possessed every place the Lord led them and touched nothing he withheld. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)

Bashan is about to be conquered, and Og the king of Bashan came out with all his people to battle at Edrei. The Most High said fear him not, for I will deliver him and all his people and his land into thy hand, as was done to Sihon king of the Amorites at Heshbon. Always remember, the battle is the Lord's; this fight is spiritual. Israel does not need weapons of mass destruction: the Bible is the weapon, and when Israel keeps the commandments the Most High fights for his people. The Lord our God delivered into our hands also the king of Bashan: they were out there doing physical war, but they gave the praise, the glory, and the victory to the Most High. They did not boast in their own swords; that is how you sanctify the Most High. The same order stands today: when you wake up you thank the Most High, and you thank him for the food even though you cooked it, because he is the one who allowed you to have it. You always put the Most High first.

Threescore cities were taken, all fenced with high walls, gates, and bars, beside unwalled towns a great many, and not one city was left untaken. They utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city, as they did unto Sihon king of Heshbon. That command came from the Most High himself; this is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of the Bible, not the invented gospel that says he loves everybody no matter what. Only the cattle and the spoil of the cities were taken for a prey; those were needed and were spared.

Israel took the land from the two kings of the Amorites on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon. Only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants. His bedstead was a bedstead of iron, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds, showing how tall and big this man was. Og was an Amorite, and the Amorites descend from Ham; [Genesis 10](/bible/genesis/10) proves the lineage. The Hamitic nations were known for great stature, as Goliath the Philistine stood nine feet nine inches, and to this day the tallest peoples on earth, the Watusi, the Dinka, and the Nilotic tribes of Sudan, Ethiopia, and Kenya, are Hamites. Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

The conquered land was divided: from Aroer by the river Arnon and half mount Gilead to the Reubenites and the Gadites, and the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half tribe of Manasseh. All the region of Argob with all Bashan was called the land of giants, because the giants there were of Og's kin, of his family. Jair the son of Manasseh took all the country of Argob and called it after his own name, Bashan-havoth-jair, unto this day.

All that were meet for the war were to pass over armed before their brethren, while the wives, the little ones, and the much cattle abode in the cities already given, until the Most High gave rest to their brethren and they also possessed their land beyond Jordan. When you read these wars, put yourself in the position of the brothers going out. Being promised victory over the land did not mean every man would survive it; Israel still had casualties, and there were brothers that gave their lives for their people. Read to understand, not just to say you read your four chapters: bring the scripture to life and visualize what was really going on.

Joshua was commanded at that time: thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings; so shall he do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest. Ye shall not fear them, for the Lord your God he shall fight for you; the victories over Sihon and Og were the proof set before Joshua's own eyes.

Moses besought the Most High: thou hast begun to shew thy servant thy greatness and thy mighty hand, for what God is there in heaven or in earth that can do according to thy works and according to thy might? That greatness shown to Moses was more than the exodus. On Sinai he received the ten commandments and the six hundred plus commandments, ceremonial, civil, moral, dietary, and sacrificial, that the Most High ordained Israel to keep. He was also told many wondrous things: the prophecies such as [Deuteronomy 28](/bible/deuteronomy/28), that the people would go into slave ships under yokes of iron, lose their nationality, become a byword and an astonishment, and that a small remnant would wake up in the end days and come back. He was shown the secrets of the times, the understanding of the parables and allegories of the scriptures, and the end itself; all of that stands behind this thanksgiving in Deuteronomy.

Moses begged: I pray thee, let me go over and see the good land that is beyond Jordan. The Most High had already told him he would not see the promised land, and Moses was trying to get him to repent of the word he had given. The sentence came from the water of Meribah: Moses said hear now, ye rebels, must we fetch you water out of this rock, and smote the rock twice. He took the credit and became high minded instead of sanctifying the Most High in the eyes of the children of Israel, so he was told he would not bring the congregation into the land. The contrast is [Deuteronomy 3:3](/bible/deuteronomy/3#v3): after the war with Og the people said the Lord our God delivered them into our hands. That is sanctifying the Most High; Moses at the rock did the opposite. The Lord was wroth with me for your sakes: Moses laid it on stiffnecked Israel. And the answer was final, let it suffice thee, speak no more unto me of this matter, as a parent tells a child that keeps begging that the matter is closed and had better not be raised again.

Get thee up into the top of Pisgah and behold the land with thine eyes westward, northward, southward, and eastward, for thou shalt not go over this Jordan; seeing it from the mountain was all that was granted. But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people and cause them to inherit the land. The Most High said plainly whom he would deal with for the crossing. Promotion comes from the Most High: he was dealing with Moses and declared who he wanted in charge, and Moses was to strengthen the man chosen to replace him.

When thou goest out to battle and seest horses and chariots and a people more than thou, be not afraid, for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. That goes for us now, because we are still in a battle. We are not physically out battling the nations as our forefathers were when they took the land; we are in a spiritual battle, for the nations are confederate against Israel being a nation any more and against our remembrance of Israel and our laws. This whole world is set up for our people to go into sin and iniquity. Fear makes people trim their ways: afraid of family at the pagan holiday table, tucking their fringes in certain places, scared to be seen in the truth. Stand boldly; the Lord has not given us the spirit of fear, for that spirit came from Satan himself.

When Israel came nigh unto the battle, the priest approached and spoke: let not your hearts faint, fear not, do not tremble, neither be ye terrified, for the Lord your God is he that goeth with you to fight for you against your enemies to save you. A lot of times you do not see that the Lord is fighting for you in the spirit; that is where faith comes in, for the Bible is a faith-based book. You have to have faith that the Most High is fighting for you, with angels encamped round about the righteous, as David told us.

The officers sent home the man that had built a new house and not dedicated it, the man that had planted a vineyard and not eaten of it, and the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her, lest he die in the battle and another man take his portion. You could very well die fighting for your people, so go enjoy these things first: dedicate your new house unto the Lord, eat the fruits of your labour from your vineyard, take your wife, then come to war for your people.

The fearful and fainthearted man was also sent home, lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart. The spirit of fear spreads: one man's fear makes the next man wonder what he knows, and soon the whole company questions the battle.

When the officers finished speaking, they made captains of the armies to lead the people, because you cannot have order without a ranking structure. Everybody cannot be calling the shots; there is one shot caller and the people follow, and that same order set in Moses' time is why a body under rank is proficient in everything it does.

When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, first proclaim peace unto it. If it answered peace and opened, all the people found in it became tributaries unto Israel and served them. In this time Israel had the power to make nations tributaries. Right now we are not even a nation, just a people with Bibles and nothing established; but wait until Christ comes, for Israel will be established as a nation again and rule the earth, and the nations will be tributaries.

Israel came to a land with terms: agree, pay the tribute, and there is peace. If the city would make no peace but made war, Israel besieged it, and when the Lord delivered it into their hands, every male was smitten with the edge of the sword. The women, the little ones, the cattle, and all the spoil of the city Israel took unto themselves and ate the spoil of their enemies which the Lord their God had given them.

That was the rule for the cities very far off. But of the cities of the nations given Israel for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth; everything had to die, from humans to animals. The Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites were to be utterly destroyed for a stated purpose: that they teach you not to do after all their abominations which they have done unto their gods, their whoredoms, their idolatry, and their wicked ways of living, so that Israel sin not against the Lord.

In a long siege the trees for meat were not to be destroyed by forcing an axe against them, for thou mayest eat of them; the tree of the field is man's life. Only the trees known not to be trees for meat could be cut down to build bulwarks against the city that maketh war with thee, until it be subdued.

verses.text: And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn into the fields, or into the vineyards; we will not drink of the waters of the well: but we will go along by the king’s high way, until we be past thy borders.

And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the villages thereof.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even unto Arnon.
And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he, and all his people, to the battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him alive: and they possessed his land.
And I sent messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
Let me pass through thy land: I will go along by the high way, I will neither turn unto the right hand nor to the left.
Thou shalt sell me meat for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink: only I will pass through on my feet;
(As the children of Esau which dwell in Seir, and the Moabites which dwell in Ar, did unto me;) until I shall pass over Jordan into the land which the Lord our God giveth us.
But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him: for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as appeareth this day.
And the Lord said unto me, Behold, I have begun to give Sihon and his land before thee: begin to possess, that thou mayest inherit his land.
Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Jahaz.
And the Lord our God delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
And we took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city, we left none to remain:
Only the cattle we took for a prey unto ourselves, and the spoil of the cities which we took.
From Aroer, which is by the brink of the river of Arnon, and from the city that is by the river, even unto Gilead, there was not one city too strong for us: the Lord our God delivered all unto us:
Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto me, Fear him not: for I will deliver him, and all his people, and his land, into thy hand; and thou shalt do unto him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
So the Lord our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.
And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many.
And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city.
But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey to ourselves.
And we took at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites the land that was on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon;
(Which Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion; and the Amorites call it Shenir;)
All the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salchah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.
To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And slew famous kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And gave their land for an heritage: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Even an heritage unto Israel his servant: for his mercy endureth for ever.
When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it.
And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.
And if it will make no peace with thee, but will make war against thee, then thou shalt besiege it:

So the Lord our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining.
And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many.
And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city.
But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, we took for a prey to ourselves.
And we took at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites the land that was on this side Jordan, from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon;
(Which Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion; and the Amorites call it Shenir;)
All the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salchah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbath of the children of Ammon? nine cubits was the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.
To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And slew famous kings: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endureth for ever:
And gave their land for an heritage: for his mercy endureth for ever:
Even an heritage unto Israel his servant: for his mercy endureth for ever.
When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it.
And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.
